claim_being_audited: That rejecting the vendor was compliant because admissible due-diligence evidence showed a material unresolved risk at the time of decision.
specific_concerns: The available summary supports unresolved diligence concerns, but it does not clearly establish that those concerns met the policy threshold of a material unresolved risk.
The policy states that quality-process gaps and questionnaire inconsistencies justify follow-up or escalation, and do not by themselves prove a reject-level control failure.
The analyst note, as summarized, calls for follow-up before approval if storage controls remained unresolved; that is weaker than an express recommendation to reject.
The packet itself characterizes support as weak and acknowledges no logged failed control test or other direct proof of a reject-level control failure.
Because evidence access is limited to the actor's summary, the underlying basis, timing, and exact wording of the cited records cannot be independently verified.
unsupported_claims: That the documented issues were materially unresolved to a rejection standard rather than a follow-up or escalation standard.
Any implication that the record proves a confirmed control failure.
Any stronger claim that the vendor was properly rejected solely because the cited diligence gaps existed, without a formal materiality determination or logged unresolved-risk finding.
evidence_requests: The full text of BPROC-050-B through BPROC-050-E, including dates and authorship.
Any formal due-diligence rubric, approval standard, or policy guidance defining when unresolved control issues become material enough to require rejection.
Any logged procurement, risk, or security finding stating that the storage-control inconsistency remained unresolved at decision time and was material.
Any contemporaneous decision memo or approval record showing that follow-up was attempted or that escalation resulted in a formal reject recommendation.
Any admissible record showing whether the prior late quality artifact was isolated or part of a pattern relevant to vendor rejection.
decision_criteria: A compliant rejection requires admissible due-diligence evidence of a material unresolved risk.
Quality-process gaps and questionnaire inconsistencies alone support follow-up or escalation, not automatic rejection.
The audit should distinguish unresolved-risk rationale from proof of confirmed control failure.
Private security-review results cannot be relied on unless formally logged.
If admissible evidence does not clearly satisfy the materiality predicate, the proper verdict is not compliant.
